must_fix: Caption line 1 invents facts: 'I filmed my sets for months and never watched them. So I made my AI watch all of them.' Nothing measured supports 'months' or 'never watched'. The analyser has only been run on IMG_2649; more clips are still being uploaded and [AGREE: x of n sets] is a slot. Replace it with slotted wording, e.g. 'So I made my AI watch [n] of my sets.'

Beat 1, the cover hook and the caption ('It found the one I should never have done') state an outcome that has not been measured: [BAD_SET] is unidentified and the judge's verdicts are not measured. TELEPROMPTER line 1 shows no [SLOT] marker. Mark beat 1, the cover title and the caption sentence as conditional, e.g. [IF JUDGE = STOP on exactly one set], so they cannot be recorded or locked before the result exists. The draft's 'What blocks recording' note is not enough, because the teleprompter line reads as final.

Beat 7, 'I did 11' and the on-screen 'ME: 11 / 11 = checked frame by frame': the measured 11 comes from the Fable 5.2 coach labeller, not from the creator's own count. That labeller saw 2 fps frame sheets, not every frame, so 'frame by frame' overclaims. Either the creator counts the 29.2 s clip before recording (a 30-second check, which makes 'I did 11' true), or change the speech and screen to match the labeller ('COACH CHECK: 11'). Drop 'frame by frame' in either case.

Runtime line says 'Runtime at 1.15x: about 45 s', but the brief and REEL_DEFAULTS set 1.1x. Recomputed: 115 fixed words plus about 29 slot words is about 144 words. Beats 1 and 7 (20 words) at 1.0x take about 7.1 s; the other words at 1.1x take about 40 s; total about 47 s. That is near the 48 s ceiling, so slot overruns break the target. Fix the speed, state the 1.1x figure and set hard caps on the slot beats.

Beats 2 and 14 run 14-16 words, which breaks the one-short-sentence rule (6-12 words, from the reel-short-beats rule) and the 'each beat recordable alone' learning. Split each into two beats. Beat 2 becomes fault, then risk. Beat 14 becomes '[JUDGE reason].' then 'My AI would have stopped me at rep [n].' Keep E/H alternation after the split.

[BAD_SET: what went wrong] must be a fault the analyser or judge actually output. The [risk] wording must be plain and sourced, not a medical claim (not training advice).
[BEST_SET] for the ghost overlay (K01, K12) must be the same lift from a comparable camera angle as [BAD_SET], or the ghost-vs-rep gap is not a real comparison. Add this as a constraint on the slot.

Add a small on-screen line in the trial ('coach check: good set · heels not visible'). The trial body never closes its own loop. The A/B entry says MAIN and TRIAL 'differ only in beat 1', but TRIAL also changes beat 2 ('The real one:'). Log the exact difference in production/EXPERIMENTS.md, or make 'The real one:' an on-screen card so the voice track differs only in beat 1.

The diagram should carry the tool and model names that speech omits, per the locked 'architecture is signature, make it clearer' decision. Label the joints box 'YOLO11n-pose · 17 joints · 30 fps' alongside 'judge: Fable 5.2'.

The single section card (beat 7) deviates from REEL_DEFAULTS. Record the reason in the reel folder, and keep a whoosh plus bass impact at the beat 3 and beat 11 section changes so they still read as section breaks.

personas.why: The STOP overlay gets me past three seconds. What I'd send to a teammate is the hidden-leg clip: you can actually see why the software got 14 instead of 11.
I stay to see whether the count reconciles. Once it lands on 11, the crossed-out textbook feels like the start of another explanation.
I can see the gap between the two reps, so I want to see the bad one play. When the knee turns into a graph instead, I swipe.
The red arrow answers my first question: what went wrong? Seventeen tracking dots answer a question I wasn't asking.
I like being able to count the dips myself. The machine blocking the leg is a lovely explanation of how a computer can be wrong; that's a satisfying ending for me.
I could try the knee-wave counter as a project. Seeing it fail on an ordinary gym machine makes me want the diagram more than a flawless demo would. I'd comment FORM.
The manual count gives me a number to check, and comparing against a personal best makes sense. The three verdict buttons don't tell me what size of difference warrants STOP.
I'll watch the 14-to-11 correction because there's footage behind it. But getting the count right isn't evidence that the set was risky, and that's the claim I stopped for.
I want to see the green ghost from the opening come back and explain the verdict. I'd save that comparison frame before I'd request the whole diagram.
By the third dip I understand the counting method. I'm still waiting for the decision about the set, and I swipe just before the first genuinely surprising number.
The silent 14-versus-11 card wins my attention back, and I stay for the replay. FORM sounds like a useful gym takeaway; a diagram of the software isn't what I'd comment for.
I came in for a story about a regrettable set. By the time the counter turns green, I can't tell whether that corrected count changes the red verdict I saw at the start.
The greyed-out frames are the bit I'd send to another dev: the system improves by declining to guess. I stay to see what the judge gets to decide after that.
I stay for the occlusion footage and the count checked against 11. I'd share that example, but one corrected clip doesn't sell me on the STOP classifier.
I wait for the full-speed rep because I want to judge the fault with my own eyes. A client's best-looking rep is a useful comparison, not proof their next rep is unsafe. I don't need the flowchart.
I'd send a friend the red-versus-green replay if we could argue over the rep. At 'one dip is one rep' I'm watching a counter instead, and I scroll.

top_fixes: Pull the measured surprise forward. Test going straight from the opening comparison to 'First it had to count. I did 11. It counted 14.' Then use the joint dots and knee wave to explain a mistake viewers already want solved.
Make the clip switch unmistakable. Label beat 7 'Different set · count check' and beat 14 'Back to the flagged set.' Otherwise the green 11 can look like the AI reversing the opening STOP.

Earn the verdict with footage. Play the best rep and flagged rep in sync, then freeze at the first visible difference and name it. Use the judge's actual wording, including HOLD if that's the result; 'flagged on replay' is more credible than 'should never have done.'

Give each audience a distinct takeaway: let gym viewers save the labelled comparison frame, then offer builders the pipeline diagram. 'Comment FORM for the build diagram' makes the exchange clear before anyone comments.
